FILTER THRESHOLD AND FIXED-RANK RECOGNITION AUDIT
7 October 2026 — /root/filter_threshold_audit

DECISION

The complementary factorial-normalized coefficient rule is correct, including
interval zeros and physical prefixes. Its sufficiency is an established-theory
corollary of Brändén–Huh, and essentially the same coefficient encoding occurs
in the new Chen–Liu paper. Sharpness is universal over replicated copies/all
totals; it is not necessity for a fixed collection, even across all totals.

Additional concrete result, developed with root: for STRICTLY POSITIVE rational
tables and a supplied physical rank, the exact complementary Lorentzian domain
is recognizable in O(m^2) rational operations and polynomial bit time. This
replaces exponential enumeration of residual patterns. Both global complement
orientations are implemented, with rejected inputs returning a quadratic
derivative witness. This recognition theorem is internally proved below; no
priority certification, counting FPRAS, or quantum compiler was executed.

Reports audited: work/cycle2/repulsive_filter_audit.txt and the parent summary.
Protocol/core/card read: work/RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.txt; knowledge 00_START_HERE.txt,
01_CORE.txt, cards/N63-projected-slater-preparation.txt (git show, no checkout
mutation). A quick personal-memory search found no relevant hits; no memory
claim was used.

1. PRECISE COEFFICIENT THEOREM

Let E_1,...,E_s be disjoint blocks, q_j=|E_j|>=1, m=sum q_j. Each nonnegative
table b_j(0),...,b_j(q_j) has interval positive support, or is identically zero.
Set beta_j(k)=b_j(k)/k!. Suppose every beta_j is logconcave, equivalently

  (k+1)b_j(k)^2 >= k b_j(k-1)b_j(k+1),   1<=k<q_j.             (1)

Then for EVERY t=0,...,m the homogeneous multiaffine polynomial

  g_t(x)=sum_[|T|=t] product_j b_j(q_j-|T intersect E_j|) x^T

is Lorentzian (zero allowed), hence logconcave on the positive orthant.
The statement has no Slater-matrix or spin-separation assumption.

Short proof and prior-art identity. Collapse all variables of E_j to y_j:

  G_t(y)=sum_[|h|=t] product_j [binom(q_j,h_j)b_j(q_j-h_j)] y^h
        =(product_j q_j!) sum_[|h|=t] product_j beta_j(q_j-h_j) y^h/h!.

The log of the normalized coefficient is a sum of one-dimensional concave
functions on a box intersected with |h|=t. For h_i>k_i choose j with h_j<k_j.

REPULSIVE FILTER AUDIT — 7 October 2026
Agent: /root/repulsive_filter_audit
Status: exact closure/interface derivations internally proved using established
Brändén–Huh results; counting/coherent-preparation conclusions still import the
new Chen–Liu FPRAS and the N63 shared-tape compiler. No FPRAS/circuit implemented.

STRONGEST RESULT

The proposed ordinary-logconcave local-table extension is valid. In fact the
complementary polynomial satisfies the required logconcavity under the strictly
weaker condition

    beta_j(k) := b_j(k)/k! is logconcave with interval support,
    b_j(k)^2 >= k/(k+1) b_j(k-1)b_j(k+1),  1<=k<q_j.          (C)

This is the maximal independently checkable LOCAL rule which works uniformly
over arbitrary copies of an admitted table and every total particle number.
It is NOT necessary for an individual collection of blocks, even if all total
particle numbers of that collection are considered. Exact fixed-instance
certification is given below.

For a two-mode site b=(1,1,g^2), (C) is g^2<=2, covering the full repulsive range
0<=g<=1 plus weak attraction 1<g<=sqrt(2). For q modes with a pair-count filter
b(k)=a^(k(k-1)/2), (C) is a<=q/(q-1). Thus amplitude g^(k(k-1)/2) is covered
when g^2<=q/(q-1). Both boundaries are sharp in the above universal sense.

The closure proof is a consequence of existing Lorentzian normalization and
polarization, not a new foundational logconcavity theorem. The application to
filtered determinant amplitudes and the exact weak-attraction boundary appear
to be additional corollaries to investigate; priority is not established.

EXACT INTERFACE

Input: explicitly supplied full-column-rank A in Q(i)^(m x r), ordered modes
U=[m], a partition U=disjoint union E_j, q_j=|E_j|, and rational tables
b_j(0),...,b_j(q_j)>=0. Each table is positive exactly on [l_j,u_j]. The total
binary input length L includes A and the tables. Require (C), or the stronger
ordinary logconcavity in the proposed claim. Empty table/support is returned
as Z=0. Matrix acquisition/variational optimization is outside the interface.

Define
  w(S)=1_[|S|=r] product_j b_j(|S intersect E_j|),
  a(S)=det(A_S) sqrt(w(S)),
  Z=sum_[|S|=r] |det(A_S)|^2 w(S).
When Z>0 the target state has amplitudes a(S)/sqrt(Z); its Born law is the
normalized summand. A full-rank A alone does not imply Z>0.

Set d=m-r and
  f_A(x)=det(A* diag(x) A)=sum_[|S|=r] |det(A_S)|
